clue.text: Some French couple in a hopeless state

parts.note: des is the French word for 'some' (plural partitive article)
a couple is a pair

explanation.surface: A French pair find themselves in a desperate situation.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is the condition of having lost all hope, a synonym for a hopeless state.

clue.text: Biblical woman acclaimed uprising with fifty involved

indicators.note: involved means the Roman numeral is wrapped up inside the reversed word
in a down entry, uprising means the word for acclaimed is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: acclaimed means hailed
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A woman from scripture is cheered amid a revolt involving fifty people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' reads the cheering word upwards, as a down entry allows; L is the Roman fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: Delilah is the Old Testament woman who betrayed Samson by having his hair cut.

clue.text: Warlord with grip on front of trigger in weapon

indicators.note: having a grip on something means holding it, so the warlord's letters hold the next piece

parts.note: a shogun was a hereditary military commander, a warlord of feudal Japan

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A warlord grips a weapon with his finger on the trigger.
explanation.definitionFit: A shotgun is a smooth-bore firearm, an example of a weapon.

clue.text: A trap, covering ace once more

indicators.note: covering means the trap word goes round the letter for ace

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap for catching game
A is the abbreviation for ace in playing cards

explanation.surface: A snare is set over an ace once again, like a card trick repeated.
explanation.definitionFit: Again is an adverb for repetition, a direct synonym of once more.

clue.text: Northern racecourse favourite getting star treatment

parts.note: Redcar is a racecourse in North Yorkshire, in the north of England
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A favourite horse at a northern track is treated like a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: REDCAR is a seaside town in north-east England with a horse-racing course.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolling out a red carpet is the idiom for giving VIP or celebrity treatment.

clue.text: Spice Girl embraced by part of UK and a foreign country

indicators.note: embraced by means the pop star's name is held inside the outer letters

parts.note: NI is the abbreviation for Northern Ireland, part of the United Kingdom
Geri Halliwell was the Spice Girl known as Ginger Spice

explanation.surface: A pop star is welcomed in Northern Ireland and abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Geri Halliwell was Ginger Spice in the 1990s British pop group the Spice Girls.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigeria is a West African nation, so a country foreign to a British setter.

clue.text: Inquisitive lad brought up easily discontented

indicators.note: in a down entry, brought up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a lad is a son

indicators.note: dis-contented means having the contents removed, leaving only the outside letters

explanation.surface: A curious boy raised to be easily dissatisfied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns SON into NOS; 'discontented' leaves the E and Y of easily.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosey describes someone prying into others' affairs, a synonym for inquisitive.

clue.text: A do singer ruined being bombastic

indicators.note: ruined means the letters of the preceding words are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A singer has spoiled a party by being pompous.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandiose means pretentiously showy or overblown, close in sense to bombastic.

clue.text: Copy businessman in charge in US city

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative, a businessman

indicators.note: the second in places the abbreviation for command inside the abbreviation for the city

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
IC is the usual short form for the person holding command or responsibility

explanation.surface: A businessman in charge of operations in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: A replica is an exact reproduction of something, a synonym for a copy.

clue.text: Put in order a shooting venue, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells the solver the phrase for the venue is to be spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a range is a place for target shooting, giving 'a range'

explanation.surface: Organise a place for target practice, so we are told.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange is to set things in a tidy sequence, synonymous with putting them in order.

clue.text: Sign exasperated expression will return in tight outfit

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac

indicators.note: will return means the exclamation is read backwards

parts.note: drat is a mild exclamation of annoyance

explanation.surface: A star sign and a cry of annoyance turn up in a figure-hugging garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A leotard is a close-fitting one-piece garment worn by dancers and gymnasts.

clue.text: Second occupant of tent in brisk run

parts.note: a camper sleeps in a tent

explanation.surface: The next person in the tent sets off at a quick pace.
explanation.definitionFit: A scamper is a quick, light run, such as a child or small animal makes.

clue.text: Very famous general abroad seen round degree ceremony finally

indicators.note: seen round means the rearranged letters are placed around the abbreviation
abroad suggests the letters wandering far and wide, so they are rearranged
finally takes the closing letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A renowned general overseas attends a graduation ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' rearranges GENERAL to LEGENAR, which goes 'round' D to make LEGENDAR; 'finally' adds the Y ending ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Legendary means celebrated to the point of being the stuff of legends, so very famous.

clue.text: Stoop in Norse figure that's pronounced

indicators.note: that's pronounced tells the solver the word for the Norseman is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a Dane is a Scandinavian, a Norseman

explanation.surface: Bend down inside a statue from Scandinavia that is notable.
explanation.definitionFit: To deign is to condescend, and to stoop is to lower oneself to doing something.

clue.text: Intuitive feeling in search unchanged

indicators.note: in signals the letters sit inside the phrase that follows, spanning its two words

explanation.surface: A gut instinct while hunting for something that has stayed the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunch is a feeling based on instinct rather than evidence.

clue.text: Loud clamour exploding near duchy

indicators.note: exploding means the letters of the following words are blown apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: A noisy uproar as something blows up near a dukedom.
explanation.definitionFit: A hue and cry is a loud public outcry, historically the shout raised to pursue a criminal.

clue.text: Make speech about loud bore

indicators.note: about means the speechmaking word goes round the musical letter

parts.note: to perorate is to make a long speech
F is forte, the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: Someone tedious delivers a noisy oration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' looks like a dull person, but it is the verb to drill. PERORATE, to declaim at length, goes 'about' F.
explanation.definitionFit: To bore a hole is to pierce it, and to perforate is to make holes through something.

clue.text: Call criminal for reserve funds?

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone
a fence is a criminal who receives and sells stolen goods

explanation.surface: Phone a crook about the money set aside.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring-fence money is to guarantee it is kept for one purpose only, i.e. to set aside or reserve it.

clue.text: Note to cut a hem not mended — like some old gear?

indicators.note: to cut means the note slices into the rearranged letters
mended means the letters are repaired into a new order

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A seamstress's note on trimming and mending an unrepaired hem on old clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mended' rearranges the three short words into MOTHEAN, and 'to cut' slips the sol-fa note into it before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Old clothes stored too long get holes chewed by moth larvae; the question mark marks the playful definition.

clue.text: Sweet wine from area consumed by gentleman sadly laid up

indicators.note: consumed by means the abbreviation for area is swallowed by the title

parts.note: Mr is the title for a gentleman

indicators.note: in a down entry, laid up means the word is placed upwards, reading backwards

parts.note: alas is an exclamation meaning sadly

explanation.surface: A gentleman, sadly bedridden, drinks a dessert wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Marsala is a fortified wine from Sicily, often sweet and used in desserts.

clue.text: Retired vicar enters function by a dining establishment

indicators.note: enters means the reversed clergyman goes inside the maths function

parts.note: tan is the tangent, a trigonometric function

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, so the abbreviation goes back to front

parts.note: Rev is the abbreviation for Reverend, the title of a vicar

explanation.surface: A retired clergyman arrives at a function beside a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' turns REV into VER, which 'enters' TAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A taverna is a small Greek restaurant or eatery.

clue.text: Two foreign articles put together for seasoned church figure

parts.note: el is the Spanish definite article
der is the German definite article

explanation.surface: Two items from abroad are combined for an experienced churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: An elder is a senior lay official in some churches; seasoned reflects the sense of older.

clue.text: Party rises unexpectedly, in brief

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: unexpectedly means the letters of the word fall into a surprising new order

explanation.surface: A party gets up suddenly, in short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in brief' looks like 'in short', but brief is a noun: a lawyer's file.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief is a set of documents on a case, and a dossier is a file of papers.

clue.text: Deny Frenchman visitor, no saint

parts.note: Rene is a typical French man's name

indicators.note: no means the saint's abbreviation is dropped from the visitor word

parts.note: a guest is a visitor

explanation.surface: Refuse entry to a French visitor who is no saint.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a variant spelling of renege.
explanation.definitionFit: To renegue is to go back on a promise, and in older use to deny or renounce.

clue.text: Bird, chicken, not caught

indicators.note: not means the cricket letter is left out of the cowardly word

parts.note: chicken as an adjective means cowardly, or craven
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A list of birds: a chicken, but not one that was caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chicken' looks like the bird, but it means cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: A raven is a large black bird of the crow family.

clue.text: Time for fewer packages?

parts.note: packages suggests parcels, but means package holidays, sold in smaller numbers outside the peak period

explanation.surface: A quiet spell for the post office with fewer parcels to send.
explanation.definitionFit: The off-peak part of the year is when travel firms sell fewer package holidays.

clue.text: One calls this eight troupers principally

definitions.text: One calls this eight troupers principally

indicators.note: principally means taking the principal, i.e. leading, letter of each of the words

explanation.surface: A group of eight performers is named this, as one might call them.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is a group of eight, such as eight musicians or performers together.

clue.text: Praise next old-fashioned sandwiches

indicators.note: sandwiches means the phrase holds the letters between its outer parts, like a filling

explanation.surface: Praise the next old-style sandwich.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise enthusiastically.

clue.text: Fruit and a lot of staple food put in container

indicators.note: put in means the shortened grain goes inside the vessel

parts.note: a pot is a container

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: rice is a staple food for much of the world

explanation.surface: Fruit and most of a staple grain are put into a pot together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' trims RICE to RIC.
explanation.definitionFit: An apricot is a small orange stone fruit.

clue.text: On retiring, skinny front of garment reveals zip

indicators.note: retiring means going backwards, so the little word is read in reverse

parts.note: skinny means thin

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: On going to bed, a skinny person's garment front reveals a zip fastener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'zip' looks like a fastener, but it is slang for zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Zip is informal American slang for zero or none at all.

clue.text: Outspoken writer of records, dealer in breakdowns?

indicators.note: outspoken, read as spoken out, signals that the writer's title is said rather than spelt

parts.note: an annalist writes annals, yearly historical records

explanation.surface: A frank chronicler of history who also deals with nervous breakdowns.
explanation.definitionFit: An analyst breaks data down into its parts; the question mark nods to a psychoanalyst treating breakdowns.

clue.text: Expand a green meandering around lake

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround the abbreviation
meandering means wandering in curves, so the letters wind into a new order

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: Make bigger a winding green round a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlarge is to make something bigger, a direct synonym for expand.
